headline: A collaborative AI laboratory reports a theory-led diamond-spin experiment
summary: A preprint reports a collaborative LLM-agent laboratory that derived and tested a calibration law for ensembles of nitrogen-vacancy spins in diamond. The agents rejected an initial design because ordinary interpolation could make the same predictions, then classified an acquisition as inconclusive when phase and reference controls failed during signal drift. Authors report that agents revised the protocol without relaxing precommitted criteria; a six-hour randomized acquisition then passed the stated controls and supported predictions on four withheld pulse sequences. These are author-reported results from one laboratory study. The public Auctopus repository’s README says its mock-model offline demo does not reproduce the paper and that study prompts are not included; experimental data and analysis are available from the corresponding author on request.
